**Reported parameter record · adopted 24 October 2026 under [#215](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/215) · record `00e77608…` · Engine `3e83e19c` · [Download exact parameters](results/selected-current-best-parameters.json)**

These are electrolyte PC-SAFT (ePC-SAFT) parameters for aqueous MEA–CO₂, with nine liquid species (CO₂, MEA, H₂O, MEAH⁺, MEACOO⁻, HCO₃⁻, CO₃²⁻, H₃O⁺, OH⁻) and five reactions R1–R5. A7 is the seventh amendment of the joint-recalibration plan in [#170](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/170); the current record is its [#212 refit](results/engine-3e83e19c-refit-chain/README.md), with MEA association volume 0.036305439.

# Adopted record and result {#working-record}

The adopted record fits 16 adjustable parameters to 307 objective rows, using native equation-of-state densities without empirical volume translation. The common calibration subset has average absolute relative deviations of 11.86% for 47 pressures and 7.10% for 94 species targets; the eight fitted Vinjarapu heats have a root-mean-square error of 1.84 kJ/mol CO₂. Of 47 fitted loaded densities, 44 meet twice their row-specific scales, and the other three are the permitted misses at 353.15 K. The largest absolute CO₂-free density error is 0.5575 kg/m³. One of four heat-capacity points exceeds the 3% comparison limit; all four pass the numerical interpretation checks.

The [phase search](results/engine-3e83e19c-phase-search/run-2/README.md) completes 162 states per fit, over 313.15–393.15 K and loading $10^{-5}$–0.6 mol CO₂/mol MEA, at 0.50, 0.80 and 0.95 of the reported-fit bubble pressure. It resolves no descent for the reported record. This finite search does not establish global stability. The [six computed limits](results/engine-3e83e19c-density-free/limits.json), density rule, complete assessments, curve checks and [307-row replay identity](results/engine-3e83e19c-paper-evidence/replay-identity.json) pass. Single local fits, active bounds and conditional uncertainty do not establish parameter uniqueness, independent physical validation, concentration transfer or absorber/stripper qualification. Independent delivered review and manuscript generator/prose updates under #211 remain pending.

# Parameters {#selected-parameters}

These tables read the [selected JSON](results/selected-current-best-parameters.json), [fit summary](results/engine-3e83e19c-paper-evidence/fit-summary.json), and [conditional uncertainty](results/engine-3e83e19c-paper-evidence/conditional-uncertainty.json). Parameter point estimates use about four significant figures; conditional standard errors use two. Hover over starred fitted estimates to see their full-precision values. Full precision remains in the linked JSON and CSV records. The [input hashes](figures/a7_regression_overview/output/parameter-table-inputs.json) identify the inputs.

[Green: a fixed charge or formulation definition]{.evidence-1} · [Blue: a numerical input with recorded qualifications]{.evidence-2}. [★](#fitted-coordinates){.fit-star} identifies fitted component or pair inputs and all 16 declared coordinates. Tied diameters and transformed chemistry are described explicitly. Green does not certify fitted properties.

Water diameter (rounded display; use the selected JSON for numerical work), with $T$ in K and $\sigma$ in Å. The constant and amplitudes are in Å; exponent coefficients are in K⁻¹:

$$\sigma_{\mathrm{H_2O}}(T)=2.78+10.11 e^{-0.01775T}-1.417 e^{-0.01146T}$$

The selected file uses solvent-density-temperature permittivity with the retained shared stage-5 water parameters. It excludes dispersion between ions with the same charge sign. For MEAH⁺ and MEACOO⁻, packing diameter is 0.88 times segment diameter and Debye–Hückel diameter equals segment diameter; Born diameters vary separately. No empirical density translation is applied. Fixed and transferred inputs carry their recorded qualifications; these tables confer no new physical validation.

R5 uses a base-10 logarithm and different coefficient units:

::: {.parameter-table .summary-table}
| Reaction | $A$ (K) | $B$ (1) | $C$ (K⁻¹) | Input owner |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| R5 · MEAH⁺ + H₂O ⇌ MEA + H₃O⁺ | <span class="evidence-2" title="">3354</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">−1.281</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">0.0004277</span> | Selected JSON |
:::

For R1–R3, $\ln K=A+B/T+C\ln T+DT+\Delta$; R2 already includes the conversion in $A$ and has no separate offset. For R4, $\ln K=A+B/T$. For R5, $-\log_{10}K=A/T+B+CT$. The displayed layouts therefore give $B$ in K for R1–R4 and $A$ in K for R5; $D$ for R1–R3 and $C$ for R5 are in K⁻¹. Other coefficients are dimensionless. R2/R5 include the fitted pivot-preserving enthalpy shifts at 313.15 K; R5 also varies its unshifted source A. The displayed reaction coefficients include these transformations and are not independent fitted coordinates or new source measurements.

<!-- CURRENT-PARAMETERS:END -->

## Bicarbonate and carbonate: source spread and bounded probes {#bicarbonate-carbonate-266}

At 30 wt% MEA and 293.15 K, the accepted parameter record falls inside the Matin–Böttinger pooled-species envelope at 18 of 19 matched loadings, separately at 101325, 500000 and 2500000 Pa. Two converged bounded probe fits preserve every fitted-group criterion but still cover only 18 of 19 points. The remaining point is loading 0.531 mol CO₂/mol analytical MEA. Its atmospheric pool is 0.0105036 mol/mol true liquid at baseline and about 0.010514 after either probe, below the envelope's lower value of 0.0114. Thus source disagreement covers most tested states, but it does not cover every state. These two local probes do not establish an unrestricted structural impossibility or a new adopted parameter set.

### Sources, conditions and quantities

Matin 2012, Method Description and Results/Discussion, pp. 6615–6617, derives speciation from titration and carbon/alkalinity balances and reports bicarbonate values above the NMR comparisons. Jakobsen 2005, Calibration Experiments and Sample Preparation, pp. 9894–9897, Table 2 and Tables A1/A2 p. 9902, separates common-peak species by calibration; its Results/Discussion warns that a species contributing below about 10% of the common signal is difficult to quantify. Böttinger 2008, §§3–7 and Table 3 p. 137, measures the common bicarbonate/carbonate signal by online NMR and fits an extended Pitzer model to speciation and vapor–liquid data. These source statements do not give a statistical uncertainty for the present inter-source difference. The reading copies and their current Zotero sources were hash-checked during reconciliation and independent readiness review. Source keys are Matin X5FACKMR/6UD2LJ7G, Jakobsen VDRXENRB/XVFDEJM2, and Böttinger E322TKPZ/TJCRKTFQ.

The [existing observation mapping](../../data/reference/MEA/manifests/speciation_linear_coefficient_rules.csv) owns the pooled quantity

$$X_{\mathrm{pool}}=x_{\mathrm{HCO_3^-}}+x_{\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}}.$$

Here each $x$ is a true-liquid species mole fraction, in mol/mol. At each of the 19 Matin loadings 0.106–0.531 mol CO₂/mol analytical MEA, linear interpolation uses only the bracketing points in Böttinger's 12-point 30 wt%, 20 °C series. The empirical scale is the absolute difference of the two source values; it ranges from 0.000418824 to 0.008 mol/mol. The envelope is their minimum and maximum. It is not a confidence interval, a standard deviation or an estimate of the fraction of model error caused by either experiment. Reported zeros remain zeros, and no source extrapolation or logarithm of zero is used.

Matin's retained condition is 293.15 K and 101325 Pa; the paper also labels ambient comparisons at 21 °C, which remains a temperature limitation. Böttinger's individual pressures are unavailable, so its observations remain outside fitting and predictions are evaluated separately at 5 and 25 bar. Those two predictions are scenarios for the same source observations, not independent experiments. The same source envelope is compared with the model at all three pressures; it is not three pressure-matched experimental envelopes.

Jakobsen remains a separate comparison. Its nominal 30 wt% preparation contains dioxane and D₂O dilution; the retained water-equivalent translation uses unloaded MEA mass fraction 0.2714274817 and measured `loadNMR`. A three-source matched spread is unavailable without a model-dependent composition correction. The nine-species model does not describe dioxane or isotope effects explicitly. Probe 2 transfers the 20 °C empirical scale across composition only to states 010–013, at loadings 0.19, 0.29, 0.25 and 0.37. Every other Jakobsen state, including 40 °C states 018–021, remains evaluation-only; [inputs.json](results/bicarbonate-carbonate-266/inputs.json) records all exclusions and source rows.

Two different carbonate fractions must remain distinguishable:

$$S_{\mathrm{pool}}=\frac{x_{\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}}}{x_{\mathrm{HCO_3^-}}+x_{\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}}},\qquad
F_{\mathrm{C}}=\frac{x_{\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}}}{x_{\mathrm{CO_2}}+x_{\mathrm{MEACOO^-}}+x_{\mathrm{HCO_3^-}}+x_{\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}}}.$$

Jakobsen state 011 has source pool 0.0008, $S_{\mathrm{pool}}=0.75$ and historical $F_{\mathrm C}=0.0190476$. The last follows the historical treatment of its blank CO₂ entry; that blank is not a measured zero. Baseline predictions are respectively 0.000801645, 0.0350537 and 0.000978759. The historical ten-point calculated/observed mean 0.0727222 refers to $F_{\mathrm C}$, not $S_{\mathrm{pool}}$. Common-peak calibration limitations apply to the split within that signal.

The historical Matin AARD of 67.4563% mixes sixteen pooled predictions with bicarbonate-only predictions for states 009, 016 and 019. Summing the retained bicarbonate and carbonate species consistently gives 67.4145%, which the present baseline reproduces. The maximum difference between those retained sums and the new baseline predictions is 7.1 × 10⁻¹⁶ mol/mol. This is a mapping reconciliation, not a physical improvement. [Historical pool reconciliation](results/bicarbonate-carbonate-266/historical-pool-reconciliation.json) retains each source file hash, both species and the legacy scalar.

### Sensitivity at fixed parameters

The Engine evaluates each positive and negative perturbation with the other parameters fixed. R2 and R3 native log-law coefficient $a$ use steps of 0.1; each interaction coefficient uses 0.01; carbonate segment diameter uses 0.01 Å, with packing/segment ratio 0.88 and Debye–Hückel/segment ratio 1 retained. Born diameter stays at 3 Å. Every fresh prediction agrees with the corresponding native coordinate evaluation within the declared numerical tolerance. The steps are diagnostic choices, not physical parameter uncertainties.

The table shows the change caused by the positive step. The Matin state is 30 wt%, loading 0.531 and 293.15 K; the separate Jakobsen state is the translated nominal-30-wt% state 015 at loading 0.78 and 293.15 K. Both model evaluations are at 101325 Pa. At state 015, baseline $S_{\mathrm{pool}}$ is 1.35695 × 10⁻⁵ versus the source value 0.0307018; the source split lies in the paper's difficult minor-carbonate range and is not fitted here.

| Perturbed quantity | Positive step | Change in Matin $X_{\mathrm{pool}}$ (mol/mol) | Change in Jakobsen $S_{\mathrm{pool}}$ (1) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| R2 native $a$ | 0.1 | 1.7689e-06 | -4.3988e-07 |
| R3 native $a$ | 0.1 | 6.5749e-07 | 1.427e-06 |
| HCO₃⁻–water $k_{ij}$ | 0.01 | 6.4321e-05 | -2.0632e-07 |
| CO₃²⁻–water $k_{ij}$ | 0.01 | 2.3643e-07 | 5.2898e-07 |
| CO₃²⁻–MEAH⁺ $k_{ij}$ | 0.01 | -5.8318e-08 | -1.595e-07 |
| CO₃²⁻ segment diameter | 0.01 Å | -1.0521e-07 | -2.3616e-07 |

For these declared steps, the bicarbonate–water interaction has the largest effect on the Matin pool at loading 0.531; R3 has the largest effect on the carbonate split at the selected high-loading Jakobsen state. These local responses neither identify unique parameters nor rank effects independently of step size. [All sensitivity values](results/bicarbonate-carbonate-266/sensitivity-values.csv) retain all states, both signs and central finite differences.

### Probe fits and preservation of the original objective

Probe 1 adds the 19 Matin pool observations, with difference residuals divided by the empirical scale and weights 1/19. Probe 2 additionally includes the four declared Jakobsen pool observations, each at weight 1/4; the scale transfer is conditional on the retained composition translation. The original 307 rows keep their construction parameters, observations, scales and weights. Each fit starts independently from the accepted endpoint. Only the six sensitivity coordinates move: R2/R3 $a$ within ±ln(10), the three interactions within ±0.1, and carbonate segment diameter within ±0.2 Å, with the stated diameter ties preserved.

Both fits converge in nine iterations with no trial failures. Fresh weighted residuals agree with the native fits to maxima of 1.59 × 10⁻¹¹ and 7.19 × 10⁻¹², below the 10⁻⁸ absolute allowance. Native and fresh total costs agree within the 10⁻⁸ relative allowance. All 326 probe-1 and 330 probe-2 predictions are available and meet their unchanged requested tolerances. The controls remain 60 iterations, 1200 seconds, function tolerance 10⁻⁸, parameter tolerance 10⁻¹⁰ and gradient tolerance 10⁻⁸. Requested Engine workers equal the full CPU count; numerical-library threads are one. Runtime files record actual elapsed times and package/input identities; no unexposed actual worker count is inferred.

### Recommendation for issue 255 stage 2 and limits

Keep Matin's pooled minor-species observations as source-disagreement diagnostics rather than automatically adding them to the adopted calibration. Keep Böttinger outside fitting under its existing unknown-pressure ruling and retain the 5/25-bar comparisons. Keep separately calibrated Jakobsen carbonate fractions, especially high-loading minor-carbonate splits, outside fitting unless a source-supported uncertainty treatment is selected. Preserve the existing qualified major-species observations and source/campaign identities. The four extra Jakobsen pool rows tested here are composition-transfer diagnostics, not an automatic promotion to active calibration data.

For stage 2, retain the consistently pooled Matin mapping and both explicitly named carbonate denominators. Carry forward the empirical envelopes and this bounded result: most points are consistent with inter-source spread, but neither of the two declared probes reconciles the last point while representing the carbonate split. The near-identical probe endpoints and active bounds warrant no parameter adoption. This is a local diagnostic comparison with measured data and numerical replay/phase verification, not independent physical validation, parameter identification, absorber qualification or evidence that every admissible model would fail.

The result uses parameter record `00e77608a8489fc9e03a7d2a86c08cb5ff782bb441368a62fa6390b8bfe9cc91` and the worktree-only merged Engine wheel `83ede7d2722d3581603f6e4139c614b8bbfc903ce90609c90b802d46eea77dd6` (`e6dae5c7`). The 307-row qualification cost is 148.87893934556408, within 6.58 × 10⁻¹⁴ relative of the retained reference. Its residual comparison allows 10⁻⁸ absolute below unit residual magnitude and 10⁻⁸ relative otherwise; predictions and total cost use 10⁻⁸ relative. The repository pin remains unchanged. [Qualification](results/bicarbonate-carbonate-266/qualification-replay.json), [source/coordinate inputs](results/bicarbonate-carbonate-266/inputs.json), [native probe 1](results/bicarbonate-carbonate-266/fit1-executed-native.json), [native probe 2](results/bicarbonate-carbonate-266/fit2-native.json), and the [diagnosis](results/bicarbonate-carbonate-266/diagnosis.md) preserve the exact inputs, wheel identities, initial refusals and owner-authorized recovery.
